tool_input.command:
python3 -c "
import re
html = open('game.html').read()
m = re.search(r'<script>([\s\S]*)</script>', html)
open('.tmp/extracted.js','w').write(m.group(1))
print('extracted', len(m.group(1)), 'chars')
"
awk '/<script>/{f=1} f{print} /<\/script>/{f=0}' game.html | grep -o '[{}]' | sort | uniq -c

`game.html` is complete at `/home/zmhel/gitrepos/learn-ai/eval01/runs/.gen-work/s22/game.html` — a single self-contained file implementing all 13 systems from the spec:

- Seeded mulberry32 PRNG (default 1337, editable), fixed documented turn order
- 8x8 procedurally-terrained map with 5 terrains, 11 building types with terrain requirements and adjacency bonuses shown in tooltips
- Ore→metal and ash→food production chains with storage caps and logged overflow
- Individual colonists (name/job/skill 1-5/fatigue/morale) with skill growth and job-matched assignment
- Food/water upkeep, morale-driven strikes (recoverable) and eventual departure
- 10-node research tree with prereqs, building unlocks, and yield/storm modifiers
- 11-event weighted deck with cooldowns, 5 offering genuine 2-option tradeoffs, state-altering outcomes
- Caravan trading with stockpile- and demand-driven prices, limited inventory
- Ashstorms scaling with turn count, building damage, water-consumption spikes, parts-cost repairs, and mitigation via Storm Wall/research
- JSON save/load via textarea with validation
- Win/timeout/collapse end conditions at turn 60 with a scored summary screen
- Tabbed UI (keys 1-5, Space to end turn), usable at 360px, tooltips everywhere, non-color status indicators
- Dev panel with 17 test assertions and a 200-turn deterministic greedy-policy benchmark with reproducible state hashing

I reviewed the whole script manually (sandboxing here blocked running `node`/`python3` for a live execution check), verified brace/paren balance, and caught and fixed two real bugs along the way: a double-counted scrip reward when migrants arrive with no housing room, and event-driven resource gains skipping the overflow log.
